action_trace.summary: Generated 10 structured interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit end-user goals (on-device deployment success criteria), pain points (current workflow gaps, hardware constraints), and acceptance criteria (performance thresholds, supported architectures). Questions decompose the requirement into user context, technical constraints, workflow expectations, and measurable success metrics to inform SRS development for the transformers on-device ExecuTorch workflow feature.

Generated 12 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (on-device deployment, performance targets), pain points (export complexity, model optimization), and acceptance criteria (inference latency, accuracy preservation, ease-of-use). Questions decompose the requirement into workflow stages (model selection → StaticCache loading → export → ExecuTorch lowering) and probe constraints (hardware targets, performance metrics, validation methods) necessary for complete requirements specification.

Interview questions decompose the on-device transformer workflow requirement using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (e2e HuggingFace→ExecuTorch pipeline), pain points (manual export friction, performance variability), acceptance criteria (reasonable out-of-the-box performance, StaticCache integration, delegate support), and boundary conditions (model compatibility, device constraints). Chain-of-Thought reasoning identifies that 'reasonable performance' is underspecified and requires concrete metrics; delegate selection and StaticCache necessity are critical design decisions.

End-users need an integrated on-device transformer deployment workflow that eliminates manual tool-chaining between HuggingFace, PyTorch, and ExecuTorch while preserving StaticCache semantics and delivering reasonable performance through automatic delegate selection. Current fragmentation creates operational friction, extends time-to-market, and requires specialized expertise.

End-users face friction converting HuggingFace transformer models to on-device ExecuTorch format due to manual multi-step processes and StaticCache loss. They require an automated end-to-end workflow preserving optimization state with guaranteed out-of-the-box performance, enabling rapid deployment without specialized infrastructure expertise or iterative tuning cycles.

End-users require a unified, automated HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline that preserves StaticCache configuration end-to-end, delivers out-of-the-box on-device performance without manual tuning, and reduces deployment complexity from specialized expertise to commodity workflow—addressing time-to-market and adoption barriers in on-device transformer deployment.

Clarification needed on performance acceptance criteria, StaticCache configuration automation, delegate selection strategy, supported model scope, failure handling mechanisms, validation requirements, and quantization format preservation to define concrete acceptance conditions for the end-to-end on-device transformer workflow.

End-user clarification questions addressing ambiguities in performance baselines, StaticCache handling across the export pipeline, delegate selection strategy, and the feasibility of achieving fully automated e2e workflow without manual intervention—critical for defining acceptance criteria and resolving conflicting expectations between 'out-of-the-box' simplicity and device-specific optimization requirements.

Clarifying seven critical ambiguities around performance baselines, StaticCache automation, delegate selection strategy, user expertise expectations, accuracy validation, model architecture coverage, and performance validation mechanisms to operationalize the e2e transformer-to-ExecuTorch workflow.

End-user requirements for streamlined on-device transformer workflow are validated and strategically sound. Three critical refinements needed: (1) quantify 'reasonable performance' with device-specific baselines, (2) define StaticCache auto-inference vs. explicit configuration strategy, (3) clarify delegate selection automation and fallback behavior. These refinements are prerequisite for moving to SRS development.

End-user confirms core workflow validity and refines three critical areas: quantified performance baselines (latency <100ms, throughput >10 tokens/sec, memory <500MB), StaticCache auto-inference with user override capability, and automated delegate selection with device capability detection. Workflow must include integrated performance validation and reduce expertise barriers through guided tooling.

End-user confirms core workflow requirement is valid and addresses expertise barriers in on-device transformer deployment. Requires refinement on three critical areas: quantified performance baselines with reference devices, StaticCache auto-inference with override capability, and automated delegate selection with device capability detection to achieve true end-to-end streamlined experience.

Consolidated 8 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue on transformers on-device deployment workflow. Validated core requirement for seamless HuggingFace→PyTorch(StaticCache)→ExecuTorch pipeline. Refined performance baselines (latency <100ms, throughput >10 tokens/sec, memory <500MB) and StaticCache auto-inference strategy. Identified 2 open clarifications: delegate automation strategy and performance improvement targets. All records conform to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability and acceptance criteria standards.

Synthesized 8 hierarchical user requirements (4 MUST, 3 SHOULD, 2 COULD) addressing seamless HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch on-device workflow. Core MUSTs: end-to-end pipeline automation, StaticCache auto-configuration with override, quantified performance baselines (<100ms latency, >10 tokens/sec, <500MB memory). SHOULDs address delegate automation, integrated validation, and documentation. Requirements traced to 6 validated interview records and 6 enduser confirmations. IR-004 (delegate automation strategy) remains OPEN for stakeholder clarification.

Targeted Deployer dialogue probing infrastructure constraints (device specs, heterogeneity, scalability across model sizes), security mandates (model encryption, weight protection, attestation), and delegate/validation strategy (accelerator detection, performance fallback behavior, benchmarking infrastructure). Questions decompose four key areas: (1) target device specifications and hard constraints, (2) security/IP protection during multi-stage export pipeline, (3) scalability across concurrent jobs and model sizes, (4) delegate automation robustness and validation infrastructure. Grounded in MoSCoW requirements (M-001 end-to-end pipeline, M-003 quantified baselines, S-001 delegate automation) and unresolved IR-004 delegate selection clarification.

Chain-of-Thought Analysis: The Deployer must clarify infrastructure readiness (device matrix, CI/CD integration), security/compliance constraints that affect export/delegate selection, scalability expectations for concurrent operations and custom delegates, performance validation ownership and variance tolerance, and technical decisions around delegate automation determinism and StaticCache metadata preservation. These answers will determine whether the seamless workflow is achievable or requires staged rollout with manual fallback paths.

Formulated 8 targeted questions for Deployer covering infrastructure baselines, security mandates, delegate automation strategy, device scalability expectations, validation integration, fallback behavior, and iteration cycle requirements. Questions probe constraints necessary to operationalize the end-to-end HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch workflow and validate performance targets against real deployment environments.

Deployer response establishes infrastructure constraints (device tier matrix, CI/CD GPU acceleration), security mandates (delegate signature validation, model integrity verification), scalability targets (support 100M-7B models, parallel compilation across 8+ configs), and operational procedures (three-stage validation, automated regression testing, fallback delegate strategy) to enable secure, scalable, cost-optimized HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch deployment pipeline meeting quantified performance baselines (latency <100ms, throughput >10 tokens/sec, memory <500MB).

Deployer response establishes infrastructure constraints (device tiers, GPU-accelerated CI/CD, <100MB runtime footprint), security mandates (delegate signature validation, sandboxing, provenance tracking), scalability targets (100M-7B parameter support, adaptive caching, auto-delegate selection), and operational procedures (performance SLA enforcement, StaticCache auto-configuration with user override, delegate guidance, comprehensive documentation) to enable secure, performant on-device transformer deployment via HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline.

Deployer response establishes infrastructure constraints (device tier matrix, runtime footprints, GPU-accelerated CI/CD), security mandates (delegate signature validation, sandboxing, artifact integrity), scalability targets (automated delegate selection, performance baselines, regression testing), and operational procedures (StaticCache auto-configuration with overrides, integrated benchmarking, end-to-end documentation) to enable seamless HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline with out-of-the-box performance (<100ms latency, >10 tokens/sec throughput, <500MB memory) on target devices while maintaining cost efficiency.

Five clarification requests raised to resolve operational ambiguities in delegate automation strategy, target device tier specifications, StaticCache constraint handling, CI/CD infrastructure readiness, and delegate security validation scope. These gaps must be resolved before Deployer can validate infrastructure feasibility and establish deployment constraints per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148.

Five operational clarifications required to close IR-004 and deployer constraints: (1) delegate selection automation strategy with fallback definitions, (2) StaticCache mismatch handling policy with performance thresholds, (3) complete device tier matrix with per-tier baseline variance, (4) CI/CD GPU acceleration alternatives and export SLA targets, (5) delegate security validation timing and sandboxing scope. Chain-of-thought: requirements specify automation outcomes but lack operational mechanisms; infrastructure constraints define constraints but not trade-off boundaries; security mandates lack enforcement timing. Clarifications enable concrete implementation strategy.

Five critical operational clarifications required to operationalize iReDev workflow: (1) delegate selection automation mechanics and fallback chains, (2) StaticCache size mismatch handling strategy, (3) complete device tier matrix with per-tier performance baselines, (4) StaticCache auto-inference algorithm and metadata sources, (5) ExecuTorch delegate security distribution model. These clarifications are prerequisite for requirements validation and deployment planning per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 environment checklist.

Deployment requirements validated with three refinements: (1) StaticCache mismatch handling requires auto-reduction or rejection logic, (2) ExecuTorch delegate selection needs automated detection with explicit override and signature validation, (3) Performance validation must integrate into CI/CD as regression gates. Infrastructure constraints (device tiers, GPU agents, runtime footprints) are feasible. Security mandates (delegate validation, sandboxing) are deployment-critical. Core end-to-end pipeline (M-001, M-002, M-003) is deployment-ready pending refinements.

Deployer confirms M-001 (end-to-end pipeline) and M-003 (quantified performance baselines: <100ms latency, >10 tokens/sec, <500MB memory on iPhone 12+/Android 10+/edge devices) are deployment-feasible. Refines M-002 to implement three-tier StaticCache strategy with auto-reduction on device memory mismatch. Clarifies IR-004 by recommending automated delegate selection via device capability detection with deterministic fallback chains (iOS: Metal→XNNPACK; Android: Vulkan→XNNPACK) and mandatory cryptographic signature validation. Operationalizes S-001/S-002 with runtime delegate sandboxing and integrated performance validation. Requires GPU-accelerated CI/CD infrastructure and device tier matrix specification as deployment prerequisites.

Deployer confirms end-to-end HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline (M-001) is deployment-feasible on target device matrix with infrastructure constraints validated. Refines StaticCache auto-configuration (M-002) with three-tier strategy including graceful memory degradation. Clarifies IR-004 (delegate selection) via automated device capability detection with deterministic fallback chains and cryptographic signature validation. Validates quantified performance baselines (M-003) and mandates security enforcement (delegate sandboxing) and CI/CD GPU acceleration for production deployment readiness.

Operating environment specification for transformers_2024q3 on-device deployment: target device matrix (iPhone 12+/6GB RAM through edge/500MB+ RAM), <100MB ExecuTorch footprint, GPU-accelerated CI/CD infrastructure, cryptographic delegate validation, performance baselines (latency <100ms, throughput >10 tokens/sec), and deterministic fallback delegate selection (Metal/Vulkan→XNNPACK) to enable seamless HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline with out-of-the-box performance.
